user_prompt:
Perform research into the following topic:
Why food is discarded and how household habits, retail practices, and public policies affect waste
Write a short report on the topic (3 paragraphs).
paragraphs: Food waste is an environmental, economic, and social problem shaped by consumer habits, retail practices, and public policy. People discard food for many reasons, including spoilage, excessive purchasing, oversized portions, uneaten leftovers, and uncertainty about whether products are safe to eat. The United Nations Environment Programme estimated that approximately 1.05 billion tonnes of food were wasted worldwide in 2022, with households responsible for about 60% of the total. [[Households are the largest source of measured global food waste, making everyday consumer behavior a crucial target for prevention.|95]] However, waste is not simply the result of carelessness; busy schedules, changing meal plans, limited storage knowledge, and competing priorities can all contribute to food being forgotten or left unused.

Household routines and retail practices influence how much food is purchased, stored, and eventually discarded. Shopping without checking existing supplies, buying more than needed during promotions, and preparing excessive portions can leave perishable food unused. In contrast, meal planning, shopping lists, appropriate storage, and using leftovers can help prevent waste. [[Research reviews consistently associate food-management practices, including checking food stocks before shopping and planning purchases, with household food waste. Retailers also contribute through demand forecasting errors, strict cosmetic standards, surplus inventory, and expectations that shelves remain fully stocked.|90]] [[Retail practices that encourage bulk purchasing or emphasize abundant displays can increase waste in some circumstances, but their effects vary by product, store format, and consumer response.|75]] Date labels are another important factor: a US consumer survey found that 84% of respondents discarded food near the package date at least occasionally, while many misunderstood what the labels meant.

Public policies can help address these problems by standardizing date-label language, supporting food donations, encouraging retailers to improve inventory management, and expanding composting and food-waste collection programs. For example, clearer distinctions between safety-related “use by” dates and quality-related “best before” dates can help consumers make better-informed decisions. [[Clearer date labels and targeted consumer education are promising ways to reduce avoidable food waste, although their effectiveness depends on consumer understanding, food type, and existing habits.|70]] [[Landfill restrictions, disposal charges, and mandatory organic-waste collection may encourage waste reduction, but evidence about their direct effects on how much food households and businesses discard remains limited.|55]]

Overall, reducing food waste requires more than asking individuals to be careful: effective solutions combine practical household routines, responsible retail operations, and well-designed public policies. Coordinated action across these levels can conserve resources, reduce household spending, and make food systems more sustainable.
